Coffee-growing cooperative.policy: put 70% of the harvest income into new planting instead of half
Coffee-growing cooperative.context: What is realistic for us: cover crops, composting and resting plots could bring worn soil back in as little as 5 years instead of 15; we could put anywhere from a quarter to 70% of the harvest income into new planting (half now); paying for extra pickers could at most double the hectares a family can look after well, from 10 to 20; and shade trees and wider spacing could cut how fast cropping wears the soil by at most a third.

assumptions.note: Assumed "soil recovery time" can be brought to 3.33.

assumptions.id: hectares a family can tend pushed
assumptions.note: From a consultant's report: "hectares a family can tend" can be 30.
Assumed "coffee price" stays at 3000, as it has been.
From our records: "best yield" is about 1.2.

Kitchen fitting backlog.policy: push the crews harder when the backlog is high, so they can fit up to 1.7 times their normal pace instead of 1.4
Kitchen fitting backlog.context: What is realistic for us: we can let the crews rush to at most 1.7 times their normal pace, or not let them rush at all; a final check before sign-off could at best halve the snags on a normal job (about 1 in 10 now); we cannot find and train a fitter in under 20 weeks (about 30 now); we could have started with at most 13 crews instead of 11; and we cannot promise a fit sooner than 4 weeks after the order, because the units take that long to arrive, nor quote more than 8.

assumptions.note: Assumed "normal error fraction" can be brought to 0.0333.
From a consultant's report: "hiring time" can be 13.3.
Assumed "base orders" stays at 10, as it has been.
From our records: "jobs per crew" is about 1.

Regional specialty mushroom growers.policy: get new rooms built in 3 months instead of 6
Regional specialty mushroom growers.context: What is realistic for us: members might agree to start new rooms at no less than half the pace they do now; a room cannot be built in less than 3 months or get its first crop going in less than 2; growers could close loss-making rooms at most half again as fast as they do; and refurbishing could make a room last at most five years instead of three; refitting idle rooms could go at most half again as fast as it does; and an idle room is stripped out after no less than 2 months and no more than 8 (about 4 now).

assumptions.note: Assumed "building response" can be brought to 0.267.
From a consultant's report: "start up time" can be 1.33.
Assumed "reference demand" stays at 240000, as it has been.
From our records: "yield per room" is about 2000.

Regional ambulance service.policy: shorten the budget process so a new crew is on the road in 9 months instead of 12
Regional ambulance service.context: What is realistic for us: the budget process could be fast-tracked so a new crew is on the road in as little as 6 months instead of 12; we could review how many crews we need as often as every month instead of every three months; and the response-time target is ours to keep: we can stop moving it, or move it more slowly than now (we close a miss over about a year), but there is no sense in moving it faster.

assumptions.note: Assumed "budget delay" can be brought to 1.2.
From a consultant's report: "review time" can be 0.2.
Assumed "growth rate" stays at 0.006, as it has been.
From our records: "population" started at about 400000.

Community food bank volunteers.policy: run twice as many recruitment stalls at community fairs
Community food bank volunteers.context: What is realistic for us: we could run at most three times as many recruitment stalls at fairs as we do now, and better ways of working (pre-packing, appointment slots) could at most get each volunteer comfortably looking after 7.5 families instead of 5.

assumptions.note: Assumed "recruitment fairs" can be brought to 1.13.
From a consultant's report: "manageable load" can be 11.3.
Assumed "agency referrals" stays at 4, as it has been.
From our records: "volunteers" started at about 40.

Regional electricians' guild.policy: when work outgrows the guild, take on enough extra apprentices to close the gap within eighteen months instead of two years
Regional electricians' guild.context: What is realistic for us: we could promise to keep taking on up to three apprentices a month however slow work gets (we have never set a minimum); we could close a gap between the electricians the work needs and those we have within as little as a year instead of two; and with encouragement up to four masters in five could supervise an apprentice instead of three in five.

assumptions.note: Assumed "intake adjustment time" can be brought to 8.
From a consultant's report: "minimum intake" can be 4.5.
Assumed "Normal Work" stays at 3300, as it has been.
From our records: "apprentices" started at about 96.

Hospital contract cleaning standard.policy: pay the cleaners for 10% overtime, so each works about 176 hours a month instead of 160
Hospital contract cleaning standard.context: What is realistic for us: we could pay for overtime of up to 20%, so a cleaner works at most 192 hours a month instead of 160; recruiting and vetting could be sped up so a new cleaner starts in as little as 2 months instead of 4; the contractor could review how many cleaners it needs as often as every month instead of every three months; and the standard is the committee's to keep: it can stop lowering it, or lower it more slowly than now (it closes a miss over about a year), but there is no sense in lowering it faster.

assumptions.note: Assumed "hours per cleaner" can be brought to 384.
From a consultant's report: "hiring time" can be 1.
Assumed "original rooms" stays at 400, as it has been.
From our records: "cleaning staff" started at about 49.

Valley groundwater board.policy: put the town on permanent summer restrictions that cut what each household uses by a quarter
Valley groundwater board.context: What is realistic for us: the board could cap the combined pumping from the town's and the orchards' wells at no less than 25,000 acre-feet a year (today nothing is capped and every well pumps what it can; the golf course well would stay outside the cap); recharge ponds could put at most 3,000 acre-feet a year extra into the ground; summer restrictions could cut what each town household uses by at most a quarter; and the town could drill its wells at most 300 feet deep instead of 200.

assumptions.note: Assumed "basin pumping cap" can be brought to 16700.
From a consultant's report: "recharge scheme" can be 4500.
Assumed "rain recharge" stays at 26500, as it has been.
From our records: "groundwater" started at about 700000.
